reading.body:
Three open roles in privacy and data protection at AI companies is too small a sample to support any claim about hiring trends.

The three postings are at Harvey, OpenAI, and Figure, and they span legal counsel, research engineering, and technical program management. That spread matters more than the count. Privacy work at AI companies is not one job. It sits in legal, in research, and in program management at the same time, which suggests the function is being staffed from several directions rather than consolidated under one owner.

Two of the three are remote, and the listed locations are Dublin, San Francisco, and San Jose. Nothing here connects to compute, buildings, or power. Privacy hiring is driven by regulation and data handling, not by data center siting or grid capacity, and the data offers no basis for linking the two.

What this does not tell you is volume, trend, or comparison. Three postings collected on one date cannot show whether privacy hiring is rising or falling, and the source list includes aggregators and company boards whose coverage of this function is unknown. Treat it as a snapshot of who is hiring for what, not as a measure of demand.
